merged_body:
Rustdoc intra-doc links in native/angr/src (updated angr-z3672, 2026-08-11). THREE authoring rules:
(1) A bare [`method_name`] never resolves — rustdoc only resolves names in *module* scope, so associated items need [`m`](Self::m) or [`Type::m`].
(2) An outer `///` doc comment on a `mod x;` DECLARATION makes rustdoc resolve *every* fragment of that module's docs — including the `//!` block inside x.rs — in the scope of the DECLARING module, not x's own. So `super::` shifts up one level and bare in-module item links break, silently, in a file you never touched. This was the root cause of 46 of the 100 warnings (run_loop_{single,steady,wave,worker} + scheduler, all declared with outer docs in exploration/mod.rs). Fix used: keep the module doc in the file's `//!` header and demote the declaration-site comment to plain `//`. Never pair an outer `///` on `mod x;` with a `//!` block in x.rs.
(3) Targets that can NEVER resolve under cargo doc — `#[cfg(test)]` items, `macro_rules!` names, items private-by-module — get a plain code span; never widen visibility just to make a doc link resolve. Note the *linking* item's visibility matters too: a `pub fn` doc linking to a private sibling trips `private_intra_doc_links` even though the target exists (5 of the angr-xtjm8 9: filesystem/ops.rs alloc_fd/offset_position, state/process.rs round_alloc_size). A pub(crate) linker with a pub(crate) target is fine. The crate-root `//!` block counts as public docs, so it may not link into pub(crate) modules at all.
GATE: --document-private-items is load-bearing (angr-sqfj8.144) — nearly every item here is pub(crate)/private, so without it rustdoc visits almost none of the docs and the lane passes with 83 broken links in the tree. Do not drop it.
LOCAL GATE (angr-z3672): the lane no longer lives only in CI. .claude/hooks/cargo-check-stop.sh runs the exact ci.yml command after clippy, under the same 'only when .rs files are dirty' guard — ~4.3s warm on the dev profile, ~0.3s when unchanged. That closes the regrowth loop this class kept riding (the box has no GitHub network, so CI never fires here). Do not remove it without replacing it in tools/ralph-gate.sh.
REFINEMENT of (3) re macro_rules! (angr-5mnx3.8): a `macro_rules!` name is resolvable by intra-doc links, but only TEXTUALLY AFTER its definition — callbacks/mod.rs has had [`with_callback_fields`] links resolving fine for months at sites below the macro_rules! block. Adding the same link to the file's `//!` module header (textually FIRST, before the definition) fails with 'exists in this crate, but it is not in scope at this link's location' — AND that one failure makes rustdoc re-report every other link to the same name, so a one-line doc edit can surface N errors at lines you never touched. Do not chase those; fix the out-of-scope one (demote it to a plain `code span!` per rule 3) and the rest go quiet.
SCOPE (angr-pr0tj, 2026-08-28): the gate is `cargo doc --workspace`, not `--manifest-path native/angr/Cargo.toml`. It was pinned at the latter in BOTH ci.yml's `Rustdoc link check` step and .claude/hooks/cargo-check-stop.sh, so the workspace's other member, native/angr-macros, was never documented and the pub `MergePolicy` derive's two links to the private VALID_MERGE_POLICIES / MECHANICAL_MERGE_POLICIES consts (a textbook rule-3 violation) sat red from the day it was written. Rules (1)-(3) apply to every member crate, not just native/angr/src. CI's clippy lane never had this hole — it runs from the repo root with no --manifest-path — and since angr-h3tx0 the Stop hook's clippy matches it. Keep any new gate command workspace-scoped so a member crate is covered on arrival. CARGO SUBTLETY the angr-h3tx0 measurement turned up: a --manifest-path-pinned clippy is NOT wholly blind to the other member — a workspace path dependency is not --cap-lints'ed, so angr-macros' *lib* was linted all along. What --manifest-path loses is --all-targets reach: only the pinned package's test/bench/example targets are selected, so a warning inside angr-macros' #[cfg(test)] mods, tests/compile_fail.rs or the trybuild ui harness scored 0 errors pinned and 2 workspace-wide. The same asymmetry does NOT hold for cargo doc, which never visits a dependency's docs at all — which is why the rustdoc half of this hole was total and the clippy half was partial.
VISIBILITY ADDENDUM to (3) (angr-f9pct): --document-private-items makes rustdoc *document* private items but does NOT make them *linkable* from outside their privacy scope — intra-doc links use ordinary Rust name resolution, so [`crate::exploration::helpers::extract_args_with_abi`] fails with 'no item named helpers in module exploration' because `mod helpers;` is private to `exploration`. Second, distinct failure mode: a link that DOES resolve but whose target is less visible than the documented item trips rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links (e.g. pub `add_constraint_raw` -> private `install_constraint`). Both classes get a plain code span; never widen visibility and never add a per-site #[allow].

merged_body: RustExplorationManager::load_snapshot_bytes (exploration/manager_methods_snapshot.rs) replaces self.sm WHOLESALE, so every manager-level field that describes the PRE-restore exploration must be torn down there by hand. Current teardown inventory: steady_config_guard() (drains a live steady session first), pending_callbacks, pending_parallel_bounces, current_stepping_state_id (angr-ph300.21), skip_hook_stack (angr-0jh0j.12), plus a policy.on_state_removed() notify loop over the outgoing STASH_ACTIVE ids (angr-0jh0j.13). RULE: any NEW transient/pending manager field (mod.rs, outside self.sm) must be added to that list — 'it auto-expires' is not an excuse. skip_hook_stack was the counterexample: its (addr, expiry) tokens expire on expiry <= self.steps, but self.steps is manager-level and is NOT rewound by a restore, and must_run_serial() reads the stack with a bare is_empty(), so a leaked entry forced the restored session serial and could silently skip a same-address hook once. Coverage test: load_snapshot_clears_the_pre_restore_pending_world in manager_methods_snapshot_tests.rs — extend it rather than adding a sibling. SYMMETRY framing: dump_snapshot_bytes calls steady_config_guard() + flush_parked_bounces_to_active() before serializing self.sm, so load must equally run the guard and clear the pending set BEFORE swapping self.sm — otherwise the next run() finalizes the OLD steady session into the RESTORED stashes (two explorations merged) and a parked need_callback can resume a discarded pre-load state. Python-side regression: test_load_snapshot_clears_parked_pending_callback in test_manager_core.py (parks a callback via symbolic SimProc arg, asserts pending_callback_ids() empty post-load).

merged_body: Z3 interns constants BY NAME, so a symbolic BV's *name* is its identity in the solver — the Rust-side RustBV::Symbolic.id does NOT disambiguate. RustBV::from_parts (native/angr/src/symbolic/value.rs) lowers the name straight to z3::ast::BV::new_const, so any two RustBV::symbolic() calls that stringify the same name produce the SAME solver variable, even across unrelated states/contexts. Consequence: every fresh-symbol mint site must suffix a process-globally-unique token. Use SymContext::new_bv(base, width) (native/angr/src/symbolic/bv_id_ops.rs) — it appends next_id(), a process-global atomic, and mints exactly one id for both the name and the .id. A per-call or per-build local counter is NOT sufficient (angr-03vl4.41: SymbolicMemory::load_concrete_or_unconstrained and build_balanced_ite_load_after_prep both restarted at 0 per ITE-tree build, so the first unmapped leaf of two builds aliased). SymbolicMemory::unconstrained_read_value shows the other acceptable shape: a file-local process-wide AtomicU64. Grep for RustBV::symbolic( with a format! name when reviewing new code. SYSCALL/PROCEDURE SIDE (angr-8o7w): native syscall handlers hit the same trap — two time()/stub calls on one path minted with a fixed name are solver-equal (ret1!=ret2 UNSAT), unlike claripy BVS. Use syscalls::support::fresh_symbolic(ctx,prefix,width) (appends procedures::symbol_counter(prefix)) for a plain mint, and procedures::fresh_zero_extended_symbol(state, prefix, src_bits, ext_bits) for the 'unconstrained value narrower than the C return type' shape (rand: 31->32, system: 8->32). ext_bits is the TOTAL target width for RustBV::zero_extend, while claripy's zero_extend takes the count of ADDED bits — why the Python procs read zero_extend(sizeof(int) - 8) for the same thing (angr-6cp06.13). Test solver-distinctness (assert ret1!=ret2 is SAT via a fresh z3::Solver), NOT just distinct RustBV ids.
